description: Approval gate enforcement at Executor Step 5. Verifies gate fires only when both handler is configured and module declares requires_approval=true, and that all four result statuses map to the correct outcomes. Since D-96 (spec v1.50.0) the three `governance_sources` cases state the module and descriptor declarations SEPARATELY: the original `module_requires_approval` boolean could be satisfied from either source, so all three SDKs passed it while disagreeing about which one decides.

test_cases.description: Gate is skipped entirely when no ApprovalHandler is configured
Gate is skipped when handler is configured but module does not declare requires_approval=true
Gate fires and allows execution when handler returns approved
Gate fires and raises ApprovalDeniedError (APPROVAL_DENIED / HTTP 403) when handler returns rejected
Gate fires and raises ApprovalPendingError (APPROVAL_PENDING / HTTP 202) when handler returns pending with approval_id

The live module instance declares requires_approval and the registry descriptor does NOT. PROTOCOL_SPEC 7.4 step 2 binds annotations = module.annotations and step 3 tests THAT binding, so the gate MUST fire. apcore-rust decided gate firing from the descriptor and ran this ungated (D-96) -- an approval bypass that every SDK's suite and this very fixture passed, because the single `module_requires_approval` boolean let each driver satisfy it from whichever source it preferred.

The registry descriptor declares requires_approval and the live module does NOT. Per D-96 the gate fires on the UNION of the governance sources an implementation has, so this MUST gate too. Reading only the module would simply invert the previous bypass: both single-source readings are fail-OPEN, and on an approval gate the failure direction is the whole argument -- requiring an approval that was not needed costs a prompt, skipping one that was needed is a bypass. An SDK whose descriptor is DERIVED from the module (apcore-python, apcore-typescript) cannot set these two independently; its driver sets the union it can express, which reaches the same expected outcome and is why the union costs those SDKs nothing.
Neither source declares requires_approval, so the union is empty and the gate MUST NOT fire. Pins the negative half: a fix that gates on everything would pass the two cases above and is caught here.

driver_contract.no_http_status: This fixture used to declare `expected.http_status` (403 / 202) and no driver asserted it, because none can: no SDK exposes a mapping from an error code to an HTTP status, and that is deliberate. `protocol-spec.md` §7.5 and §8.2 annotate 47 framework codes with an `http_status`, but the MUST there is "define the following error TYPES" — the status is descriptive metadata for whoever puts an executor behind HTTP, not a required SDK surface. A conformance fixture may only declare what a driver can assert (apcore#94).
